subject: Post-demo follow-up: Dedicated capacity edge cases & traffic shape clarifications
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Park <emma@olive.ai>; Daniel Morris <dan.morris@olive.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo follow-up: Dedicated capacity edge cases & traffic shape clarifications

Hi Emma / Daniel —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and a few targeted questions so we can size a Dedicated pool that matches both your steady-state and burst patterns. I pasted a short bullet summary below and then a handful of clarifying asks — answers will let us recommend a GPU flavor + pool sizing and an ops fallback ladder (hosted -> dedicated fallback behaviors).

Summary from call
- Primary use case: real-time chat & summarization for customer support transcripts (low latency requirement at 95th pct).
- Two traffic modes: steady inbound (about 150 rps) and short bursts (~2k rps for 30–90s during product launches).
- Current hosted eval shows token mix centered on 60–400 tokens per response; occasional long-form generation up to ~1200 tokens.
- Security: must run in a private VPC for PII-sensitive customers but willing to pilot on Dedicated hosted pool first.

Clarifying asks (helps pick GPU family / concurrency / quantization):
1) Can you confirm avg vs peak tokens-per-request? You mentioned 200–400 typical but saw longer tails — can you share a percentile distribution (p50/p90/p99) if available?
2) For the burst profile: is the 2k rps input measured as unique requests/sec or inference calls after frontend batching?
3) Target latency: what is your SLO for p95 token-latency or end-to-end response time? (e.g., 200ms p95 / 500ms p95)
4) Any hard restrictions on GPU family? (H100 preferred for large-batch throughput, A100 for cost balance, or do you need Ampere-class compatibility for on-prem hardware?)
5) Will you accept quantized model variants (int8 or 4-bit) for cost savings at slight quality delta, or do you need FP16 single-precision only?

Next steps I propose:
- If you can share a small throughput spreadsheet (p50/p90 token lengths, avg tokens, percent of long runs >800 tokens) we'll run a quick capacity simulation and return a recommended pool (GPU count, concurrency per GPU, expected sustained TPS and burst headroom).
- Schedule 30m follow-up with Karthik (cc'd) to walk through the simulation and ops considerations.

Attached: blank throughput template (olive_throughput_profile.xlsx) — fill what you can. If you'd rather, paste a few sample traces in the reply.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0218

Hi Soojin —

Thanks for the clear recap. We filled out the throughput template (attached) and added our current architecture diagram for context. High-level answers inline below, and attached file has per-endpoint token histograms.

Answers to your asks:
1) Token distribution (from our logs): p50=180, p90=420, p99=980. Mean tokens/request ~230.
2) Burst profile: 2k rps is measured at the frontend before batching. Our frontend batches up to 8 reqs into one inference call during bursts.
3) Target latency: goal is 300ms p95 end-to-end for the chat endpoint; for summarization we can accept 700ms p95.
4) GPU family: Our infra team prefers H100 for cloud pilots (we already use H100 in other workloads), but our on-prem team currently has A100s — would like guidance on a common denominator if we want the same model weights across environments.
5) Quantization: we are open to int8 for most customers but need FP16 or higher for premium enterprise customers.

Attached: olive_throughput_profile.xlsx, current_arch_diagram.pdf

We'll book the follow-up with Karthik — Daniel, can you join the sizing call?

Best,
Emma Park

Hi Emma —

Thanks for the spreadsheet, that helps a lot. Quick read and a few operational notes before our call:

Operational reads from the attached histograms
- p99 ~980 tokens means long-tail sessions will drive KV cache sizes and per-inference memory. For H100 we'd recommend planning for larger sequence models or chunked decoding.
- Frontend batching of 8 during bursts implies the serving layer will see up to ~250 effective inferences/sec per GPU at high concurrency if you pack well.

Initial sizing hypotheses (ballpark)
- Option A (latency-first): H100s, 6 GPUs in a Dedicated pool with 16-concurrency per GPU tuned for low p95; autoscale policy to add 2 GPUs at ~70% sustained utilization. This targets ~1.2k steady-state through the pool with burst headroom and per-request latency near your 300ms p95 for chat (depends on model variant).
- Option B (cost-balanced): A100s, 8 GPUs with 20-concurrency per GPU and quantized int8 models for baseline customers and FP16 for premium. Expect slightly higher p95 but better $/token.

Questions for the call we should be ready to answer
- Which endpoints need strict p95 SLOs vs those tolerant of higher latency? (You mentioned chat vs summarization.)
- Is model switching by customer tier acceptable (int8 vs FP16)? If so we can recommend a mixed pool strategy and routing rules.

I'll prepare an initial simulation and share a one-pager with expected TPS per-pool and rough monthly cost ranges. Marissa — will route a proposal & early-term pricing after the sizing call.

Thanks,
Karthik
Principal Solutions Eng | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
